newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DUTCH ENTREPRENEUR REVIVES FOKKER HOPES.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH ENTREPRENEUR REVIVES FOKKER HOPES.

text.p: The Dutch owner of Belgian regional airline VLM is preparing to resurrect bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker Fokker, VLM said on Wednesday.

"The chance (Fokker could re-start) is one out of four," VLM chief executive officer Freddy Van Gaever told Reuters after a news conference on a cooperation deal between Vlaamse Luchtvaart Maatschappij and Deutsche Lufthansa AG .
He said VLM owner Jaap Rosen Jacobsen was ill and could not attend the news conference "because he has been working day and night for the past two months to try and start up Fokker again".
"If (Jacobsen) succeeds in restarting Fokker, VLM will be one of the first ones to buy new planes," Van Gaever told the news conference.

Receivers said earlier this month they would begin liquidation of Fokker, bankrupt for over a year, with sales of non-fixed assets. Two Dutch firms plan to hold a series of private sales and auctions this autumn.
VLM currently has seven Fokker 50 aircraft and has ordered two more. Three of the seven turboprop planes currently owned are leased to Spanish independent regional airline Air Nostrum.
